2024_202_course_description_book_2024_20.paragraph: The Troy School District 2024-2025 Course Description Book, revised January 2024 under Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky, catalogs the courses offered at Athens High School and Troy High School together with graduation requirements, curriculum flexibility options, Oakland Schools Technical Campus programs, and the district anti-discrimination grievance procedure. All students must earn a total of 22.5 credits to be eligible for a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma, including 4.0 credits of English, 4.0 of mathematics, 3.0 of science, and 3.0 of social studies. Beginning with the class of 2028, a 0.5-credit personal finance requirement is embedded in Economics.
2024_202_course_description_book_2024_20.page:
**Publication**
2024-2025 Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School, Troy School District. Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Revised January 2024.

**Schools and contacts**
- Athens High School: Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085. Main Office 248.823.2900, Fax 248.823.2913, Counseling 248.823.2962, Attendance 248.823.2901.
- Troy High School: Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098. Main Office 248.823.2700, Fax 248.823.2713, Counseling 248.823.2715, Attendance 248.823.2701.
- Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221. Central Office Special Education: 248.823.5096.

**Nondiscrimination**
The book opens with the district policy of nondiscrimination citing Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the District Director of Special Education serves as Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**Graduation requirements, Classes of 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028**

| Requirement | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| Personal Finance | 0.5 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE | 3.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Online Learning Experience | 0.0 |
| Total credits needed for graduation | 22.5 |

Science differs by cohort: the classes of 2027 and 2028 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5 and Physics 0.5, Earth Science 0.5, and a Science Elective 0.5; the classes of 2025 and 2026 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0, and a Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics comprises Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 (or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B, or CTE program completion), and a math elective, with a required math experience in the final year. Social studies comprises World History/Geography 1 and 2, American History/Geography 1 and 2, Economics, and Government and Civics. The World Language / Fine & Applied Arts / CTE block requires 2.0 World Language credits, or 1.0 World Language plus 1.0 CTE or 1.0 VPAA. The online learning requirement is a 20-hour non-credit experience embedded in Troy classes.

**Flexibility options**
Updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b. Options include the Personal Curriculum, a Physical Education elective waiver for students completing two seasons of district athletics or two seasons of marching band, World Language flexibility for heritage or international proficiency, and CTE program completion credits exchanged on a 1:1 basis for science, world language, or the Algebra 2 requirement.

**Departments covered**
Business, Career Technical Education, Industrial Technical, Life Skills, English, English Language Development, Fine Arts, Health, Mathematics, Media, Physical Education, Science, Social Studies, Special Education, and World Language.

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus**
OSTC-SE at 5055 Delemere Street, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, serves juniors and seniors on a selective basis, generally 1.5 credits per semester. Session 1 AM is course 08101 and Session 2 PM is 08102; morning classes begin 7:50 AM and dismiss 10:20 AM, afternoon classes begin 12:00 PM and dismiss 2:30 PM. Where regular students carry six credits, OSTC students carry three credits at their home high school plus three at OSTC. Applications are made online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. Credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved.

**Grievance procedure**
A three-step formal anti-discrimination grievance procedure is filed with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, beginning with a written grievance submitted within 10 workdays of the incident and ending with a final and binding written answer from the Superintendent.
2024_202_course_description_book_2024_20.verbose:
The 2024-2025 Course Descriptions book for Athens High School and Troy High School, issued by the Troy School District under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, and revised in January 2024, is the district catalog of high school course offerings, graduation requirements, curriculum flexibility provisions, career-technical options, and civil rights procedures.

POLICY OF NONDISCRIMINATION. The opening statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act, and states the district does not discriminate on the basis of sex or handicap. A grievance procedure is available through any school office, and employees in a bargaining unit may alternatively use the collective bargaining agreement procedure. In accordance with federal regulations, the district has appointed Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, as Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the District Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

SCHOOL DIRECTORY. Athens High School is led by Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, at 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085, with Main Office 248.823.2900, Fax 248.823.2913, Counseling 248.823.2962, and Attendance 248.823.2901. Troy High School is led by Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, at 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098, with Main Office 248.823.2700, Fax 248.823.2713, Counseling 248.823.2715, and Attendance 248.823.2701. The Department of Teaching & Learning is at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221. Central Office Special Education can be reached at 248.823.5096.

GRADUATION REQUIREMENTS, CLASSES OF 2025, 2026, 2027, AND 2028. English requires 4.0 credits: English 9 (1.0), English 10 (1.0, class of 2028 and after), English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 and 2 (1.0), and English 12 Lit/Comp 1 and 2 or 12 English AP 1 and 2 (1.0). Science requires 3.0 credits, with different pathways by cohort: for the classes of 2027 and 2028, Biology 1.0 credit, Chemistry 0.5 credit and Physics 0.5 credit, Earth Science 0.5 credit, and a Science Elective 0.5 credit; current requirements for the classes of 2025 and 2026 are Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0, and Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics requires 4.0 credits: Algebra 1 (1.0), Geometry (1.0), Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B (1.0, or met through CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a Math Elective (1.0); students must have a math experience in their final year of high school. Social Studies requires 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1 and 2 (1.0), American History/Geography 1 and 2 (1.0), Economics (0.5), and Government and Civics (0.5). Personal Finance is 0.5 credit embedded into Economics and becomes a graduation requirement beginning with the class of 2028, contingent on taking a TSD Economics or AP Economics course. Physical Education requires 1.0 credit: Intro to Physical Activity (0.5) and a P.E. Elective (0.5). Health requires 0.5 credit, and the same block lists 1.0 credit VPAA, which includes Industrial Technology, Business, and Life Skills classes. State Assessments carry 0.0 credit but require completion of Michigan-required assessments administered during high school. The combined World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, and CTE requirement is 3.0 credits, satisfied by 2.0 credits of World Language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 credit of World Language plus either 1.0 credit CTE or 1.0 credit VPAA. The Online Learning Experience is 0.0 credit but requires a 20-hour online learning experience embedded across middle and high school. Credit-bearing high school courses taken before high school matriculation appear on the Troy School District high school transcript with grades earned. Total credits needed for graduation are 22.5 for either a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma. Courses may be retaken prior to or concurrent with the next course in sequence, with the retaken grade replacing the initial grade unless prior administrative approval is granted.

GRADUATION REQUIREMENT FLEXIBILITY OPTIONS, updated 9.2015 and citing MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b. The Personal Curriculum allows additional credits in some core academic areas in lieu of other requirements when aligned to the student Educational Development Plan (EDP). The Physical Education Elective option excuses students participating in two seasons of Troy School District athletics or two seasons of marching band from the 0.5-credit P.E. elective, tracked automatically with no forms required. The 2.0-credit World Language Requirement has flexibility for non-English heritage language proficiency, international study and residence proficiency, and substitution of CTE or Visual & Performing or Applied Arts credits, documented through a Personal Curriculum. CTE Program Completion permits a 1:1 credit exchange toward science, world language, or the Algebra 2 requirement. A course key explains that descriptions begin with the course number and title, note the school if not offered at both, and give grade levels, length, credit, retake rules, and prerequisites; no course may be retaken for additional credit unless specifically indicated, except Independent Study.

BUSINESS DEPARTMENT. Accounting and Finance offerings are 005002 Accounting 1, 005022 Accounting 2, and 005122 Financial Management, each one semester and one-half credit, and each satisfying one-half credit of the math-related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year. Business Administration Management + Operations includes 005415 Business Law + Management, 005404 Digital Business (Microsoft Office, WordPress, Canva, Microsoft Office Specialist Program certification), 005231 Business Entrepreneurship, 105033/205033 Junior Business Field Study Co-op (requires 10+ accumulated credits for junior status), 105043/205043 Senior Business Field Study Co-op (requires 14.5+ credits for senior status; up to 2.0 credits for at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester of work experience), 005272 Web Creation 1, and 005282 Web Page Creation 2. Marketing offerings are 005222 Marketing 1, 005226 Marketing 2, 005223 Honors Marketing (preparing for the CLEP Principles of Marketing examination), 005182 Sports and Entertainment Marketing including a Troy Athens Fantasy League, 005113 School Based Enterprise for 12th grade only, and 105213/205213 Marketing Field Study Co-op with up to 2.0 credits.

CAREER TECHNICAL EDUCATION. Education Occupations includes 007393 Careers in Education 1 and 007403 Careers in Education 2, using the Troy Athens Preschool located within Athens; advanced placement credits are offered at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College, and Davenport University, and completing both courses makes students eligible for the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Hospitality and Food Services courses operate the newly renovated Terrace Cafe restaurant lab at Athens: 007384 Restaurant Operations / Terrace Cafe (2 semesters, 2 hours, 2 credits), 007373 Commercial Baking, and 007473 Commercial Foods, all using the ProStart food service curriculum with eligibility for a national certificate of achievement and the ServSafe Sanitation Certificate. Automotive offerings at Troy High are 007003 Automotive Technology 1, 007294 Automotive Tech 2 (a 2-hour block class with 2 retakes), 007213 Automotive Technology 3, and 007413 Automotive Technology 4, with instruction meeting NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards. Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2, and 3 are 007163, 007173, and 007183.

INDUSTRIAL TECHNICAL DEPARTMENT. Offerings include 108713/208713 Mechatronics 1, 108723/208723 Mechatronics 2, 007072 Architectural Drawing 1, 007082 Architectural Drawing 2, 007122 Game Design 1 (Athens, primarily Java), and 007102 Game Design 2 (Athens).

LIFE SKILLS DEPARTMENT. Courses are 007242 Parenthood/Child Development 1 and 007262 Parenthood/Child Development 2, both eligible for advanced placement credit at Oakland Community College; 009862 Essential Skills for Adulthood; 007272 Personal Money Management; 007292 Foods and Culture (Troy High); 007282 Foods 2 (Troy High); 007332 Fashion Design 1 and 007342 Fashion Design 2 (Troy High); 007372 Stitchery (Troy High); and 007283 Interior Design (Troy High), which uses AutoCAD.

ENGLISH DEPARTMENT. Core sequence courses are 101043/201043 English 9, 101053/201053 English 10, 100073/200073 10 Honors English Literature/Composition, 00082 11 English Literature/Composition, 100443 11 English AP 1, 200443 11 English AP 2, 000113 12 English Lit/Comp, and 000453 12 English AP 1 & 2. Electives include 000182 Creative Writing 1, 000192 Creative Writing 2, 000232 Classical Mythology and Drama, 000212 Film and Literature, 000312 Literature of Suspense, 000382 Science Fiction, 000132 Voices in Literature, 000322 Sports Literature, 000352 Personal Communication, 000392 Speech 1, 000142 Speech 2, 000492 Debate 1, 000502 Debate 2, 000242 Modern Shakespeare, 100273/200273 Writing for Publication: Journalism, 000333 Writing for Publication: Newspaper, 000343 Writing for Publication: Yearbook, 000342 Writing for Broadcasting, 000362 Advanced Writing for Broadcasting, 000353 Advanced Publication Production, 00252 Seminar AP, and 002533 Research AP, which culminates in an academic paper of approximately 4000-5000 words with an oral defense.

ENGLISH LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT. Initial placement is determined by the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol, and the state requires annual administration of the WIDA ACCESS. Courses are 101013/20103 Beginner ELD, 101023/201023 Intermediate ELD, 101033/201033 Advanced ELD, 101113/201113 Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs, and 101103/201103 EL Tutorial (graded pass/fail). Language Support content classes offered on a rotating basis are 104703/204703 LS Biology, 004322 LS Chemistry, 004313 LS Physics, 002272 LS World History/Geography 1, 002282 LS World History/Geography 2, 102703 LS American History/Geography 1, 202703 LS American History/Geography 2, 002092 LS Government/Civics, and 002422 LS Economics.

FINE ARTS. Visual Arts include 006212 Multi-Media Art, 006201 Mindful Art, 006232 Drawing 1, 006243 Advanced Drawing, 006252 Painting 1, 006263 Advanced Painting, 006352 Cartoons, Comics & Animation, 006272 Ceramics 1, 006283 Advanced Ceramics, 006362 Lettering & Calligraphy, 006373 Studio Art, 006393 Advanced Art AP, 006222 Applied Arts and Design, 006422 Computer Graphics 1, 006433 Advanced Computer Graphics, 006292 Sculpture, 007112 Principles of Photography 1, and 007114 Advanced Photography. Music includes 006023 Campus Band, 006013 Concert Band, 006143 Cadet Band (Troy High), 006003 Symphonic Band, 006033 Jazz Ensemble, 006042 Jazz Explorations, 006002 Color Guard, 006104 Percussion, 006083 Freshman Orchestra, 006073 Concert Orchestra, 006063 Symphony Orchestra, 006093 Philharmonic Orchestra (Troy High), 006113 Treble Choir, 006103 Concert Choir, 006123 Mixed Chorus (Athens), 006133 Madrigal Singers (Athens), 006132 Chorus/Choir Accompanist, 006053 AP Music Theory (which counts as a math elective credit for seniors who have completed all other required math credits), and 006501 Intro to Music Technology and Recording using ProTools. Theatre Arts includes 000402 Theatre I, 000412 Theatre II, 000422 Theatre III, and 000162 Youth Theatre.

HEALTH DEPARTMENT. 008852 Health is required for graduation and covers healthy lifestyles, violence, sexual harassment, nutrition, fitness and weight control, alcohol and drug abuse, tobacco, human sexuality, birth control, and sexually transmitted diseases including HIV/AIDS. 008573 Peer Mediation is a grade 12 course requiring a recommendation from the Peer Mediation teacher.

MATHEMATICS DEPARTMENT. Offerings are 003043 Algebra 1, 103123 Intensified Algebra 1 (a double-blocked 2-hour course), 003063 Geometry, 003930 Geometry Honors, 003263 Algebra 2 Part A, 003273 Algebra 2 Part B, 003093 Algebra 2, 003183 Algebra 2 Honors, 003233 Precalculus, 003253 Precalculus Honors, 003023 College Algebra, 003173 Calculus AB AP, 003203 Calculus BC AP, 003213 Statistics AP, 003212 Calculus 3 and 003222 Linear Algebra (both Dual Enrollment with Lawrence Tech), 003142 Computer Science 1, 003163 AP Computer Science A, 003373 Computer Science Principles AP, Cybersecurity listed as 003172 at THS and 103172/203172 at AHS, and 103383 Introduction to Data Science using the Pyret programming platform.

MEDIA DEPARTMENT. 008492 Media Center Services, 008502 Media Center Techniques, 008682 Innovation Learning, and 008692 Innovation Lab, the latter influenced by the D school at Stanford University and referencing creatinginnovators.com and dschool.stanford.edu. 002523 Seminar AP and 002533 Research AP also appear here.

PHYSICAL EDUCATION. 007952 Intro to Physical Activity Level 1 and 007962 Level 2, one of which is required for graduation and includes CPR training, physical fitness, swimming testing, and team sports; students cannot take both for credit. Other courses are 006162 Exercise and Lifelong Fitness, 006172 Self Defense and Lifelong Fitness, 008082 Net Sports & Fitness, 005511 Fall Team Sports & Fitness, 005512 Spring Team Sports & Fitness, 007922 Weight Training and Aerobics Fall, 007912 Weight Training and Aerobics Spring, 005515 Beginning and Intermediate Tumbling & Gymnastics/Fitness, 005521 Learning to Swim, 005522 Lifeguarding/Advanced Swimming (students must be 15 years old; certification cost is $40), and 008014 Fall / 008024 Spring Strength and Conditioning. The President Challenge Physical Fitness Test is given in most physical education classes, and one credit of physical education is required for graduation.

SCIENCE DEPARTMENT. 004003 Biology, 004053 Anatomy and Physiology, 004063 Genetics, Bacteriology, Biotechnology, and Embryology, 004073 Advanced Placement Biology, 004122 Chemistry 1, 004123 Chemistry 2, 004243 Chemistry 2 AP, 004102 Organic Chemistry, 004231 Physics 1, 004232 Physics 2, 104236/204236 Engineering Physics, 004253 Physics 2 AP, 004263 Physics C AP, 004314 Environmental Science: Human Impact, 004212 Astronomy, 004042 Forensic Science, and 004273 Environmental Science AP, which satisfies the Earth Science requirement.

SOCIAL STUDIES DEPARTMENT. 002232 World History/Geography 1 (from the collapse of Rome to the French Revolution and defeat of Napoleon), 002503 Human Geography AP, 102023 American History/Geography 1 and 202023 American History/Geography 2 (covering the United States from 1877), 002013 American History/Geography AP, 002062 Economics, 002073 Economics AP, 002072 Government and Civics, 002052 Government AP, 002242 World History/Geography 2, 002233 World History/Geography AP, 002152 Psychology 1, 002162 Psychology 2, 002163 Psychology AP, 002182 Sociology, 002112 Mental Health, 002082 Philosophy, 002042 Comparative Government and Politics AP (core countries China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria, and Russia), 002322 Political Science, 002032 History of American Criminal Law, 002034 History through Film, 002502 Conflicts of the 20th & 21st Centuries, 002122 Introduction to Leadership, 002125 Leadership Lab, 002222 LINK, 002523 Seminar AP, 002533 Research AP, 106383/206383 AP Art History (investigating 250 works of art), and Stories of Yourself & Others, a grade 12 interdisciplinary course earning one-half ELA credit and one-half History credit through the lens of Reconstruction history.

SPECIAL EDUCATION DEPARTMENT. Achievement Skills courses are 109909/209909 (1A/1B, 9th grade), 109910/209910 (2A/2B, 10th grade), 109911/209911 (3A/3B, 11th grade), and 109912/209912 (4A/4B, 12th grade), all for students certified by an IEPT. Other courses are 009273 Linguistics 2D, 009283 Linguistics 2E, 009263 Linguistics 2F, 009201 Reading Strategies, 003003 Integrated Math 1, 003103 Integrated Math 2, 009303 English Language Arts 1, 009573 English Language Arts 2, 009332/009342 Math Skills A/B, and 009632/009642 Life Skills Math. Placement is made in collaboration with the IEP case manager.

WORLD LANGUAGE DEPARTMENT. French is 000603 French 1, 000613 French 2, 000623 French 3, 000633 French 4, and 000643 French AP. Spanish is 000693, 000703, 000713, 000723, and 000733 Spanish AP. Japanese is 000823 Japanese 1, 000833 Japanese 2, 000843 Japanese 3, 000863 Japanese 4, and 008863 Japanese AP; students read and write 120 basic Kanji characters by the end of Japanese 2, another 170+ Kanji in Japanese 3, and another 180+ Kanji in Japanese 4. Chinese is 000853, 000873, 000883, 000893, and 000813 Chinese AP. German is 000653 German 1, 000663 German 2, 000673 German 3, and 000683 German 4. All sequences are benchmarked to the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, progressing from Novice-mid/Novice-high in level 1 to Intermediate-high/Advanced-low at the AP level, and AP examinations are given in May.

OAKLAND SCHOOLS TECHNICAL CAMPUS. OSTC-SE, an extension of the home high school, is located at 5055 Delemere Street, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, with a Southeast Campus in Royal Oak, MI and a Northeast Campus in Pontiac, MI. Programs are offered to grades 11-12 on a selective basis, with OSTC recommending high school credit based on the local district requirement, generally 1.5 credits per semester. Session codes are 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM; morning session classes begin at 7:50 AM and are dismissed at 10:20 AM, and afternoon session classes begin at 12:00 PM and are dismissed at 2:30 PM. Where regular students carry six credits, OSTC students must carry three credits at their home high school in addition to three credits at OSTC. Programs listed include Automotive Technology (must begin in 11th grade), Collision Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security), and Cosmetology (must begin in 11th grade). Buses transport students to OSTC-SE and back; afternoon-session students must provide their own transportation home. Sophomores and juniors may apply for the following year, with an exploration tour in the fall and online application at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. A note warns athletes that credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved.

ANTI-DISCRIMINATION GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE. Any student or employee who believes he or she has been discriminated against, denied a benefit, or excluded from participation on the basis of sex (including sexual harassment), race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status, or handicap files a written grievance with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator; forms are available in the Employee Services Department. Step 1: the written grievance form goes to the immediate supervisor or administrator within 10 workdays of the incident; not later than the next workday a copy goes to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services; within 5 workdays of the filing date the supervisor meets the grievant; within 3 workdays of the meeting a written answer is given. Step 2: appeal within 3 workdays of receipt of the answer to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, a meeting within 10 workdays of receipt of the appeal, and a written answer within 5 workdays of that meeting. Step 3: appeal within 3 workdays to the Superintendent, a meeting within 10 workdays of receipt of the appeal, and a written answer within 5 workdays of the meeting, final and binding on all parties. A grievance not filed or appealed within the time limits is deemed abandoned; failure to hold a meeting or render a decision allows automatic appeal to the next level; time limits may be extended only by mutual written agreement; records are confidential and none is kept in a staff member personnel file if the final decision is that there was no reasonable basis for the grievance.
